messages:
Sam: Heads up — during the canary a bunch of function-call schema rejects spiked but they were mostly from a single integration. We need a way to show soft-degraded vs hard-rejects in the dashboard.
Anya: Saw that. Are you talking about the strict validator flag we rolled out?
Sam: Yeah. Strict mode emits a hard reject (500-ish) for contract mismatches. We also have soft-degrade path that returns the model output but marks it. The telemetry currently lumps them together.
Ben: Can we split by route + validator_level in the sampling pipeline? Right now the sample tag gets dropped at the metric exporter.
Jo: We should also surface quota implications — soft-degraded responses still bill differently and customers are confused. Dashboard needs a clear legend.
Anya: Agreed. Proposal: add two series to the panel — `fncall_rejects{type="hard"}` and `fncall_rejects{type="soft"}` and a third stacked series for `fncall_degraded_served`.
Sam: +1. Also want a column in the recent-requests table with `validation_outcome` so SRE can click through.
Ben: Implementation notes — exporter currently maps validation_outcome to an int. We need to change to string label, which will increase cardinality. Concern: Prometheus label explosion.
Jo: What if we emit a high-level label for metrics (clean/soft/hard) and keep the detailed reason in logs/events? That reduces label dim.
Anya: That works. For troubleshooting we can link to the sample index and keep full rejection reason there.
Ben: Another thought: sampling bias. The problematic integration is high-volume; if we sample uniformly we miss rare causes. Need stratified sampling by integration_id.
Sam: Good call. Can we add a high-volume sampler override for `integration_id` with a small reservoir?
Ben: Yes. Implementation: router tags `route_id`, exporter tags `integration_id` and `validator_level`, sampler runs before metrics sink.
Jo: UX ask: show a heatmap of top (route_id, validator_level) pairs and a toggle to only show canary vs global.
Anya: Also add an annotation when we flip strictness for a route so dashboard shows the event.
Sam: Who owns the dashboard changes? Eng-platform or DevEx?
Jo: Eng-platform builds the metrics and panels. DevEx can polish wording and add runbook links. @devex-bot can you create a doc stub with suggested copy?
devex-bot: Created doc: https://internal.docs/redwood/observability/fncall-validation-ux — stub added, please review. :white_check_mark:
Ben: For rollout plan — start with a permissive canary for 48h, enable sampling and heatmap, then flip strictness in small percentage increments (10/25/50) while monitoring `fncall_degradation_rate`.
Sam: Can we make the canary auto-fallback if hard_reject_rate > 0.5% for 10m?
Anya: Yes, we have the feature flag runner that can do rollbacks. We'll wire an alert to the flag controller.
Jo: I’ll add dashboard panels for the alert thresholds and a link to the flag runbook.
Sam: One last thing — billing. Product asked for a separate meter for soft-degraded tokens so they can show customers breakdown. Add `billing.soft_degraded_tokens` to the usage pipeline.
Ben: That will need a follow-up on the billing ingestion contract, but doable.
Jo: Action items: Ben — change exporter labels + implement stratified sampler (owner). Jo — update dashboard panels + annotations (owner). Anya — add flag rollback and alerts (owner). Sam — run canary and notify customers. DevEx — polish doc copy.
Sam: Thanks all. I’ll kickoff the canary after the exporter PR lands.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for eng-platform/exporter#142 — review required.
Sam: pinging reviewers — please take a look today, aiming to ship metrics change before 12:00 UTC tomorrow.
